sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the western part of Boonton's town centre at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 30 degrees so that the streets run square to the page. Cedar Street crosses near the top and Birch Street across the middle, with Oak, Green and School Streets running down the sheet and Liberty Street cutting diagonally from the lower left towards the top. Brook Street forms the right-hand margin, where the sheet meets sheet 3, and Main Street runs along the bottom beside the Morris Canal and its incline railway. The upper blocks are mostly frame dwellings on regular lots, with a rectory and Sisters Home beside the Church of Our Lady of Mt. Carmel, a Roman Catholic church shown in blue as fireproof construction. Below Birch Street, the Boonton High School and the Graded School stand off School Street, the latter lettered Boonton Public School, and the Harris Lyceum with a stage and vacant stores lies at the corner of Main Street. Along Main Street the frontage is continuous with stores, an auto sales room, a garage, the Mansion House hotel and a print shop, and the C. A. Hagan and Son bottling works stands on the canal side. Water pipes of 4 and 8 inches are lettered along the streets, hydrants are dotted, and the street widths are marked in feet. Plane Street leaves Main Street at the bottom right. Block numbers 17 to 24 are printed, and the adjoining sheet numbers 3, 5, 9 and 10 stand in the margins. A compass rose with a north arrow pointing up and to the left is drawn in the upper right.
notes: Brook Street is today Boonton Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Liberty Street and Green Street keep their names; the drawn street widths are 45 to 50 feet.
Fitted at about 8.0 pixels per foot, which agrees with the printed 50 ft scale.
50 ft. Boonton centre west of sheet 3: Cedar, Birch, Main, Oak, Green, Liberty, School, Brook (Boonton Avenue). One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of Boonton's business and residential district at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 30 degrees so that the streets of the town grid run square to the page. It shows the blocks between Cedar Street at the top and Plane Street at the bottom, and between Brook Street on the west and William Street on the east, with Church Street and Cornelia Street running down the sheet and Birch Street across its middle. Main Street crosses the lower part of the sheet and is lined on both sides by brick and frame stores, many with dwellings or offices above, a bank, a hall and a motion picture theatre. The Borough Hall with the jail and the fire department stands on Main Street near Brook Street, and the Holmes Library is at Church and Main. The blocks north of Main are residential, with frame dwellings on narrow lots and a few larger institutional buildings: St. John's Episcopal Church on Cedar Street, the First Presbyterian Church and its chapel on Church Street, and the First M. E. Church with an adjoining garage near Main and William. Below Main Street, along Plane Street, are tenements, a machine shop of P. Whitehead with its power and heating notes, and stores backing onto the street. Water pipes of 4, 8 and 10 inches are drawn along the streets with their sizes, and hydrants are marked. Union Street is lettered just beyond William Street at the east edge, where the sheet meets sheet 4; sheets 2, 4, 5 and 11 adjoin on the other sides.
notes: Brook Street is today Boonton Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Streets are lettered without suffixes except Union St.
50 ft. Pilot. Downtown: Cedar, Birch, Main, Plane, Brook (now Boonton Avenue), Church, Cornelia, William. One part. Detector defaults.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the eastern side of Boonton's business district at 50 feet to an inch, with the town grid turned counter-clockwise on the page. Cedar Street runs along the top, Birch Street across the middle and Main Street along the bottom, and Union, Mechanic and Division Streets run down the sheet between them. William Street and a fork of Union Street appear at the left edge where the sheet meets sheet 3. At the right the double-track railroad passes through the sheet from the top to Main Street, where it crosses the Morris Canal on a stone bridge. Two passenger stations stand beside it, with a wagon shed, a coal trestle and a signal tower, and Myrtle Avenue runs parallel to the tracks. Morris Avenue leaves Main Street and runs down to the canal at the bottom. The upper blocks hold frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a row of brick-coloured dwellings near Cedar and Mechanic Streets. Main Street is lined with brick and frame stores, among them the Lathrop Building, the Hotel Boonton, the Post Office, a bakery with a portable oven, a restaurant and lodging house, an undertaker, a large garage and an auto sales building, with feed storage, blacksmith shops and a trucking garage on the west side of Mechanic Street. Plane Street branches off at the lower left, and the American Legion post is at the lower right. Geo. L. Salmon's sales and exchange stables stand at the right edge. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 10 inches are lettered, and a compass rose and north arrow are at the left.
notes: The north arrow points about 32 degrees left of up and the fit gives about 38 degrees, a few degrees more than sheets 2 and 3 (about 30).
Street names match OpenStreetMap: Union Street, Mechanic Street, Division Street, William Street, Morris Avenue and Myrtle Avenue.

50 ft. Boonton centre east of sheet 3: Cedar, Union, Mechanic, Division, Birch, Main, Plane, Morris Av, Myrtle Av; D.L.&W. R.R. and stone bridge over the canal. Fits about 8 degrees from sheet 3 but agrees at shared junctions (0.7 and 2.5 m).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the industrial strip along the Morris Canal and the Rockaway River south and west of Boonton's centre at 50 feet to an inch. Main Street and Plane Street run from the upper centre to the lower right, with the Morris Canal incline railway, its flume and the canal basin beside them, and School Street and Brook Street join them from the north-east. The upper left holds the ruined works of the Boonton Chemical Corp. and the New Jersey Light and Power Co. power station with its engines, wheel pit and gate house. Below them stand the Geo. Benda works for bronze powder, with water wheels, mill ponds and sprinkler systems, and the Louis Sacks sash weights foundry, all on the estate of J. Couper Lord, which is leased as a whole by the Jersey Corporation. In the centre the Hubbard Oven Works and a large old and vacant factory building lie above a belt of railroad tracks that curve across the sheet and run off the left edge. The lower half is mostly open ground crossed by 6 and 8 inch water mains, with a vacant building and a concrete structure marked old and vacant at the bottom. The Rockaway River crosses the lower left corner and the Morris Canal turns past bridges at the lower right, where the Geo. Benda ware house stands. Water pipes, hydrants and an embankment are lettered. A compass rose with a north arrow pointing up and to the right is at the upper right, and block numbers 2, 3 and 7 are printed at the edges.
notes: Brook Street is today Boonton Avenue (OpenStreetMap).

The part has no street grid; it is anchored on two hand-picked junctions, Main Street / School Street and Boonton Avenue / Main Street, with scale (8.0 px/ft) and north (24 degrees) taken from the config. The second junction agrees with the first to about 2 m.
50 ft. Industrial strip on the Morris Canal and Rockaway River below Main and Plane: no street grid; anchored on Main / School Street with a check point at Boonton Avenue / Main (2.1 m).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 lies south-west of Boonton's centre at 50 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned about 24 degrees. The right half holds a residential district between West Monroe Street at the top and Harrison Street at the bottom, with Lincoln Street and Washington Street running down the sheet and Grant Street crossing between them. The houses are small frame dwellings with a garage, an auto repair shop and a gas holder near Monroe Street. The Morris Canal appears at the top right, crossed by a bridge, and Lathrop Avenue leaves at the upper right corner. In the middle the Pelgram and Meyer silk throwing mill stands on the east bank of the Rockaway River with its engine room, silk vault, coal bin and storage, and a steel bridge carries West Monroe Street across the river. The left half is occupied by the Boonton Rubber Mfg. Co., with Buildings Nos. 1 to 4, a press room, a finishing room, mixing and shipping buildings, a machine shop, a pipe shop and storage, laid out along a heavy railroad line and rail tracks lettered D. L. & W. R.R. along the left edge, and a Tile Mfg. building (Building No. 1) at the lower left. The sheet is marked Vacant, No Exposure along its top margin. A compass rose and a second north arrow point up and to the left. Block numbers 18, 25 to 29 are printed, and sheet numbers 4, 12 and 13 stand in the margins.
notes: Street names agree with OpenStreetMap (Monroe Street, Lincoln Street, Washington Street, Grant Street, Harrison Street, Lathrop Avenue).
The sheet is drawn at about 8.0 pixels per foot, as the 50 ft scale bar indicates.
50 ft. South-west Boonton: Monroe, Lincoln, Washington, Grant, Harrison, Lathrop Av; Boonton Rubber Mfg. Co., silk mill. One part.

sheet-7-1.description: Sheet 7 of the March 1924 Boonton atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the southwestern edge of the town, where the built-up streets give way to open ground south of the Rockaway River. The main map fills the sheet except for the inset box in the top-right corner (the freight depot area, which is a separate part). Essex Avenue runs down the left edge. Dover branches from it near the top and runs south-east to meet Reserve, and Reserve then bends south-east across the sheet as a wide street with a pipe line, finally meeting Morris Avenue at the lower right. Rockaway runs south-east along the river, parallel to Reserve, and is crossed by South Lane. North Lane is a short street between the two diverging roads at the top. The blocks between Dover, Rockaway and Reserve (numbered 164 and 165) are laid out in narrow lots with only a handful of dwellings, while the larger blocks east of Rockaway and South Lane (166 and 167) hold a row of frame dwellings along the curving street. Most of the left and centre of the sheet is block 163, a large undeveloped tract with scattered dwellings and the Pudding Stone Inn, a steam-heated hotel reached by a dashed drive. Block 214 and 215 at the top left are subdivided lots along Essex Avenue. The Rockaway River curves down the upper right with a compass rose beside it. At the lower right, Morris Avenue runs north-east past dwellings beside the steep embankment of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western railroad tracks. Water pipe sizes and distances to the next street are marked along the streets.
notes: Dover joins Essex Avenue at today's Fairview Avenue junction (modern name inferred from the fit, not printed).
The Rockaway Street / Morris Avenue junction in OpenStreetMap lies about 18 m east of the junction drawn on the sheet, so it was left out of the control points.
Part 2 of this sheet (the inset in the top-right corner, showing the D.L.&W. freight depot and Morris Avenue) has no street junction and is not georeferenced.
100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Essex Av, Dover, Reserve, Rockaway, North and South Lane, Morris Av, Fanny Rd); 2 inset top right, D.L.&W. freight depot.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset top right: D.L.&W. freight depot at Morris Avenue (no street junction (Morris Avenue crosses the railroad on a bridge); needs points carried from sheet 5 or 12 (step 6b)).

sheet-8-1.description: Sheet 8, part 1 covers the west side of Boonton along West Main Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The Mountain Lakes Manufacturing Company inset in the top-left corner belongs to another part and is left out of this one. West Main Street crosses the sheet from the lower left, where it meets Elcock Avenue and Schultz Avenue near block 154, towards the upper right, where it passes Chestnut Street and Lake Avenue and leaves the sheet at Essex Avenue. Chestnut Street and Lake Avenue run north from West Main Street across blocks 142 and 143 to River Street. The north half of the sheet is a lightly built residential district of small dwellings, many with outbuildings, on long narrow lots. A dash-dot boundary line crosses the wooded block 141 and is marked as the borough limits; a similar line appears near Elcock Avenue. Water-pipe lines of 4 inches run along several streets and fire hydrants are marked. South of West Main Street the blocks 155 and 156 hold more dwellings and a few small buildings, with woods behind. Dover Street is shown as not open across the lower part of the sheet, between the woods blocks, and a second Dover street runs in at the lower left. Reserve Street crosses the bottom edge. Essex Avenue runs down the right side with Rockaway Street entering from the east. Large parts of the lower and left areas are blank or wooded and marked as no exposure at the sheet edge, where the neighbouring sheets continue. A lone institutional building in block 160 is coloured pink.
notes: No OpenStreetMap junction matches the drawn Elcock Avenue and West Main Street junction (Elcock Avenue and Schultz Avenue appear to be part of Powerville Road today), so the west third of the part has no control points.
Printed 'River' corresponds to River Road today.
Dover Street and Dover (not open) are not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name.
Street names read from the 1600 px overview and full-resolution crops of part of the sheet; the small print along Elcock Avenue was not read letter by letter.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main, west Boonton (West Main, Chestnut, Lake Av, Elcock Av, Schultz Av, Dover, Essex Av, Reserve, River, Rockaway); 2 inset top left, Mountain Lakes Mfg. Co. lumber yard on the Denville and Pine Brook Turnpike (US 46) at the Boulevard, Mountain Lakes.

sheet-8-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 8 is an inset in the top left corner of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch, showing the plant of the Mountain Lakes Manufacturing Company, a lumber yard and mill work, in Mountain Lakes, some distance south-west of the main map of the sheet. The Denville and Pine Brook Turnpike, 60 feet wide, runs diagonally down the inset from the top to the lower right corner, where the Boulevard leaves it. Along a railroad siding parallel to the turnpike stand the company's buildings: a lumber warehouse, a sash and lumber warehouse, a woodworking machinery building with hose notes, a dry kiln and boiler house, an office, lumber sheds and a platform, with scattered piles of lumber across the open ground to the west and a fire protection note for the plant. Near the Boulevard are the temporary plant of the Standard Bitulithic Company, an auto repair shop and a few small buildings. The inset is outlined by a heavy line, and the labels 21 show that it adjoins sheet 21.
notes: The Denville and Pine Brook Turnpike is today US 46, a divided highway; placed from a hand-picked Boulevard / US 46 junction at the sheet scale, with north set to 47 degrees from the turnpike and Boulevard directions (the inset's arrow points straight up). Low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main, west Boonton (West Main, Chestnut, Lake Av, Elcock Av, Schultz Av, Dover, Essex Av, Reserve, River, Rockaway); 2 inset top left, Mountain Lakes Mfg. Co. lumber yard on the Denville and Pine Brook Turnpike (US 46) at the Boulevard, Mountain Lakes.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 of the March 1924 Boonton atlas, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the north-western part of the town between the Rockaway River and the Morris Canal. The principal feature is the long diagonal belt of the river and canal down the left side of the sheet, with a cemetery and a few outbuildings on the west bank beside Lake Avenue. Across the water, North Main and Hill streets run north-west to south-east through blocks 145 to 149, with Birch, Summit and Cedar Avenue parallel to them further east, all cut by Highland Avenue and by the Addison and Pine cross streets. Hillside Avenue curves along the upper left corner next to the borough limits. The lower centre shows the downtown edge of Boonton: Main Street runs east along the north bank of the canal, West Main Street crosses the river and canal on a steel bridge and a canal lock is marked beside it, and Essex Avenue runs south from the bridge approach through an area of woods (block 157) to Rockaway Street at the bottom. Dwellings are mostly frame, with a few stone and brick ones, and Boonton's Slavish Union Hall, a Slavish Roman Catholic church, St. Mary's R.C. school with St. Joseph's Hall, tenements and an auto repair shop are lettered. Sunset Lake lies in the top centre, and the north arrow and a scale bar for 100 feet appear near the edges. Neighbouring sheets are 8 on the left, 10 above right, 2 on the right and 7 below.
notes: Addison is marked 'Not open' on the sheet.
River Street at the left edge may correspond to today's River Road (inferred, not printed).
Birch bends from its north-west to south-east course into an east-west street east of Highland Avenue; the detector matched it to today's Birch Street.
Control points are thin in the upper left and along the river, so the placement there rests on the street grid to the east.
100 ft. North-west Boonton: Hillside Av, North Main, Hill, Birch, Summit, Addison, Highland Av, Pine, Oak, West Main, Lake Av, Essex Av, River St; Sunset Lake, Rockaway River.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 of the March 1924 Boonton atlas, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the north-eastern edge of the built-up borough. The left half is largely open: woods and hillside lots (blocks 113 to 124) lie above Oak, which runs north-west to south-east, and Woodside Avenue (New), a newly laid out street that curves from Oak north-east to Green, with Barnett and East Street branching north-west from it. The Borough Line and the 'No Exposure' margin cross the top left, and Sunset Lake with a compass rose fills the left edge. Highland Avenue, Cedar and Addison Street are drawn at the bottom left, around a few dwellings and a tenement in block 35. The right side holds the town's regular grid: Green runs south from the Woodside bend, Liberty runs parallel to it, and Wootton, Laurel, Esten, Spruce, Boyle and Cedar cross them at about 300-foot intervals, with Brook along the right edge. St. Mary's R.C. Cemetery (block 127) occupies the top centre and another cemetery lies between Laurel and Esten. North Holmes is drawn across the top of the sheet; Liberty beyond it is marked 'Not Opened'. Most lots have frame dwellings with house numbers on the street side; blocks 36 and 199 are mostly vacant. Neighbouring sheets are 9 on the left, 11 on the right, 2 below and 3 below right.
notes: Brook is today's Boonton Avenue.
Woodside Avenue (New) is today's Wootton Street where it curves south-west towards Oak Street.
North Holmes is drawn about 11 m north of today's North Street, so that street was left out of the control points.
The lower-left junctions of Oak, Highland Avenue and Cedar are skewed and were not detected, so that corner has no control point.
100 ft. North Boonton: Oak, Green, Liberty, North Holmes, Wootton, Laurel, Esten, Spruce, Boyle, Cedar, Highland Av; St. Mary's R.C. Cemetery.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 of the March 1924 Boonton atlas, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the eastern residential grid of the borough, with the industrial edge at the lower right. Four north-south streets (Brook, Church, Cornelia and William) are crossed by Wootton, Laurel, Spruce and Cedar at regular intervals, forming blocks 101 to 106 and 134 to 136 that are mostly filled with small frame dwellings, with a few stone or brick buildings, a church and a fire department building near Brook. North of Wootton the blocks (129 to 131) are thinly built, and the top of the sheet, marked 'No Exposure', is open woods where Lane and a pair of unbuilt streets are laid out. On the east side, Union, Mechanic and Division streets run south-west to north-east, and block 111 is occupied by the works of F. Drew and Company, manufacturers of oleomargarine and lard, drawn in pink with a note of its equipment (pumps, refining, steam, fire protection and sprinklers). The large block 112 and the woods east of William are blank, and a branch railroad is shown running up the right edge near Division. A compass rose is placed at the right centre. Blocks 108 to 110 in the lower right front onto Cedar and Mechanic and have small shops and dwellings. Neighbouring sheets are 10 on the left, 12 on the right, 3 below left and 4 below right.
notes: Brook is today's Boonton Avenue.
The sheet is drawn at about -29.5 degrees from north, the same grid angle as sheet 3.
The block lines east of William are drawn without street names; the streets on the right edge near Division curve from the grid.
100 ft. North-central Boonton: Church, Cornelia, William, Laurel, Spruce, Cedar, Wootton, Union, Mechanic, Division, North Holmes, Esten.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 of the March 1924 Boonton atlas, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the south-eastern edge of the borough around Lathrop Avenue. At the upper left the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western railroad yard fans out beside Division Street and Myrtle Avenue, with the lumber, coal and wood yards of Henry Salmon and Son, E. B. Dawson, and a feed mill lettered on the Myrtle Avenue frontage. The Morris Canal runs in a curve down the left centre, and Lathrop Avenue runs from the canal crossing at the lower left east and then north-east past the Lathrop Avenue High School, a hollow tile building, and north along the right edge towards Wilson and Overlook Avenue. The centre is block 1, a very large undeveloped tract, with Roesler and Kanouse streets laid out through it as rows of vacant narrow lots. In the lower left, blocks 39 to 41 hold a compact grid of small streets (Washington, Madison, Holmes, Old Boonton Road and Monroe) with Van Duyne Alley; dwellings are mostly frame, with garages and a machine shop. Maple Avenue runs between the canal and Madison. Roosevelt and Morrison avenues are drawn at the bottom right running south from Monroe. Lathrop Avenue at the right edge is lined with dwellings and the lower end of a private way branches east. Neighbouring sheets are 11 on the left, 6 and 13 below, 16 above and 15 above right.
notes: Roesler is spelled Roessler Street in current OpenStreetMap data.
The drawn Montclair Line (the former D.L.&W. line) lies about 13 m from the modern line on this sheet; no railroad control point was used.
An unnamed street labelled only 'Road' runs south-east on the right side; it is not matched to a modern street.
The upper left (Myrtle Avenue and Division) has no street control point, so its placement comes from the Lathrop Avenue and Monroe junctions.
100 ft. East Boonton: Division, Myrtle Av, Main, Washington, Madison, Holmes, Old Boonton Road, Lathrop Av, Roesler, Kanouse, Wilson, Overlook Av, Maple Av; D.L.&W. R.R. yard and Morris Canal.

sheet-13-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 13 is the main map, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 24 degrees, and covers the residential district of South Boonton. West Monroe Street and Monroe Street run along the top, with Grant, Harrison, Dixon Avenue, Dawson Avenue and Mandeville Avenue following down the sheet. Lincoln, Washington, Madison and South Holmes Streets and Old Boonton Road run across them, and Taft Street, Sherman Street, Roosevelt Avenue and Morrison Avenue lay out a newer subdivision at the right. The blocks, numbered 28 to 194, hold small frame dwellings, many with outbuildings, on narrow lots, and the density falls from the left to the right, where blocks 179 to 185 and the land beside Old Boonton Road are largely vacant. The 1st Reformed Church stands near Washington and Monroe Streets, the South Boonton Public School and the Marion Apartments lie further down Washington Street, and a woodworking shop with an electric motor stands at Dixon Avenue. Greenwood Cemetery occupies block 193 in the lower middle, above the inset box of part 2. A dashed road curves across the lower right corner, where the scale bar stands. A compass rose and north arrow point up and to the left, and block and street widths are marked in feet. The sheet adjoins sheets 6 and 12.
notes: South Holmes is today Holmes Street (OpenStreetMap).
Mandeville Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and was not used for control.
Monroe Street east of Madison Street is drawn about 30 feet wide against 50 feet in the parcels, and its junctions with Roosevelt and Morrison Avenues sit 3.5 m off the fit.
A lone road lettered only 'Road' curves across the lower right corner.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main, South Boonton (Monroe, Grant, Harrison, Dixon Av, Dawson Av, Mandeville Av, Lincoln, Washington, Madison, South Holmes, Old Boonton Road, Taft, Sherman, Roosevelt Av, Morrison Av, Greenwood Cemetery); 2 inset at the bottom at 50 ft (Harrison / Lincoln).

sheet-13-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 13 is the heavily outlined inset box at the foot of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, which enlarges the strip of Harrison Street and Lincoln Street south of Greenwood Cemetery. Harrison Street runs across the top of the box and Lincoln Street down its right side, with a 4 inch water pipe in Harrison Street and a note giving the street width as 50 feet. Lots numbered 47 to 73 front the south side of Harrison Street, holding small frame dwellings, a printing works in a long fireproof building lettered Printing, and a vacant square structure further down. The block is numbered 29 and a half and is cut across by an oblique line at the lower left. Greenwood Cemetery lies above the box, and the inset joins the area drawn on sheet 6, whose number is printed in the box beside Harrison Street. A north arrow points up and to the left in the lower part. The part has only one street junction, Harrison Street with Lincoln Street, at the edge of the box.
notes: Placed from one detected junction, Harrison Street / Lincoln Street, with scale (8.0 px/ft) and north (about -25 degrees) from the config; low confidence.
Harrison Street is drawn about 27 feet wide against 50 feet in the parcels, so the junction centre may be several metres off.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main, South Boonton (Monroe, Grant, Harrison, Dixon Av, Dawson Av, Mandeville Av, Lincoln, Washington, Madison, South Holmes, Old Boonton Road, Taft, Sherman, Roosevelt Av, Morrison Av, Greenwood Cemetery); 2 inset at the bottom at 50 ft (Harrison / Lincoln).

sheet-14-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 14 is the lower and larger part of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, south-west of the centre of Boonton where Morris Avenue meets Fanny Road beside the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad. Morris Avenue runs up the left side of the part and Fanny Road crosses it, continuing east over the railroad cutting on a concrete bridge. The four tracks of the D. L. & W. R. R. run down the middle of the part. West of Morris Avenue are the long sawtooth-roofed manufacturing buildings of the Standard Railway Fusee Corporation, makers of railroad fusees, with an office. Between Morris Avenue and the railroad stand the buildings of the Langdon McCormick Studios, makers of artcraft and period design lamps in copper, brass and bronze, including a manufacturing and shipping building, a machine shop and storage. East of the railroad is the plant of the Boonton Gas Light Improvement Company, with its retort and coal house, purifying house and two gas holders, connected to the tracks by a siding. Most of the rest of the part is open land with a few dwellings, and block numbers 163, 168 and 198 mark the surrounding areas. A heavy line separates this part from part 2 at the top of the sheet, which shows Powerville and is drawn at another rotation. Its north arrow points nearly straight up, but the fit places the streets about 34 degrees anticlockwise of that.
notes: The part's north arrow is about 23 degrees off the fitted rotation (-34 degrees); the fit rests on Fanny Road / Morris Avenue and the railroad crossing under the concrete bridge.

50 ft (scale bar). Two parts divided by a heavy line. Part 1 (lower, larger): Morris Av / Fanny Rd at the D.L.&W. R.R., Langdon McCormick Studios, Standard Railway Fusee Corp., Boonton Gas Light Improvement Co.; its north arrow is about 23 degrees off the fit. Part 2 (upper): Powerville, Field & White Co. roofing paper mill on Public Rd crossing the Rockaway River, head race and Morris Canal, Boonton Rd; north arrow about +40 degrees.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: upper part: Powerville, Field & White Co. roofing paper mill on Public Rd at the Rockaway River, head race and Morris Canal (location not matched to modern streets: Bush Road (River Road to Old Boonton Road) and Powerville Road at the Rockaway River were tried; neither fits the drawn distances (150 m between the two road junctions against 230 to 560 m); needs identification of the Powerville crossing on the ground, then parcel corners or hand-picked junctions (step 6b)).

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 of the March 1924 Boonton atlas, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the open country on the north-eastern edge of the borough, with the New Jersey Firemen's Home at the lower right. The sheet is turned: its north arrow points to the upper left, so that Lathrop Avenue, which runs south from the middle of the sheet, is drawn running down the page. Vreeland Avenue crosses the sheet from left to right at about the middle, meeting Lathrop Avenue, and Lower Montville Road leaves it at the right, running north-east to the edge. South Terrace curves down the left side and meets Vreeland Avenue at Oxford, a short street whose frontage is divided into eight lots lettered F to M and that carries a few frame dwellings. Elsewhere the sheet is mostly farmland and blocks 174 to 177. At the upper right are the greenhouses of Arthur Taylor, a long group of glass houses with a dwelling and sheds. The New Jersey Firemen's Home, a pink-coloured group of buildings with a dormitory and a reception hall, sits among lawns with two fountains, a pipe line and a fire department shed. Along the bottom edge, Wilson and Overlook Avenue run east and west, joining Lathrop Avenue at a circled water main junction; rows of small frame dwellings line them. 'No Exposure' is printed around the margin because the neighbouring ground is left to other sheets. Sheet 12 lies below.
notes: The sheet is rotated about -74 degrees from north.
Only four control points: Oxford / Vreeland, Lathrop / Vreeland and two hand-picked points where Wilson and Overlook meet Lathrop Avenue. Low confidence.
Lower Montville Road has no matching street in the reference data and was not used.

100 ft, turned on the page. East of Boonton: South Terrace, Oxford, Vreeland Av, Lathrop Av, Lower Montville Road, Wilson, Overlook Av; N.J. Firemen's Home, Arthur Taylor greenhouses. Placed from two detected and two hand-picked junctions; joins sheet 12 cleanly.

sheet-16-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 16, the lower left quarter of the sheet, is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows a stretch of Myrtle Avenue in the north-east of Boonton, where the avenue runs beside the four tracks of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad on their way towards Montville. Myrtle Avenue crosses the bottom of the part diagonally, with a 4-inch water pipe along it, and the railroad runs parallel to it on the north-west side, with a siding curving away to the west. Between the two stand the long buildings of the Zamium Corporation, makers of acid resisting alloy, marked closed, and the fireproof building of the Boonton Molding Company, makers of molded insulation, with its sprinkler and power notes. A small machine shop with a tile roof stands near the avenue at the south-west corner of the part, and the same building is drawn on sheet 12, which adjoins here. The rest of the part is open land, with block number 3. A heavy line separates it from part 1 above, which shows Myrtle Avenue further north at another rotation, and from part 3 to the right, which shows Montville.
notes: Placed from a corner of the machine shop carried from sheet 12 (anchored, sheet scale, north set to -20 degrees so that Myrtle Avenue follows the local direction of its modern line); a second corner carried from sheet 12 is a check. Low confidence for rotation.
The north arrow points straight up; on this atlas the arrows of the inset parts are not reliable.

50 ft. Three parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (top): Myrtle Av with the Van Raalte Co. silk mill and Standard Oil Co., Boonton. Part 2 (lower left): Myrtle Av with the D.L.&W. R.R., Zamium Corp., Boonton Molding Co. Part 3 (lower right): Montville, Boonton Rd (Main Road) at Sioux Rd (River Road), Morris Canal and plane railway.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: upper part: Myrtle Avenue with the Van Raalte Co. silk mill and Standard Oil Co. (no street junction and no feature identified on a placed neighbour; drawn about 24 degrees from the modern line of Myrtle Avenue; needs parcel corners of the Van Raalte site or a feature shared with sheet 15 (step 6b)).

sheet-16-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 16, in its lower right quarter and drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up, shows the centre of the village of Montville, a few kilometres east of Boonton. Boonton Road comes in from the west along the bottom of the part and turns north, crossing the Morris Canal on a bridge and curving away to the north-east, while Sioux Road, marked as an arbitrary name, continues south from the turn. The Morris Canal crosses the part from south-west to north-east with a foot bridge, and the inclined plane railway of the canal runs parallel to it to the south. A creek with a small pond and dam enters from the north-west and joins the canal, and another stream runs past the junction to the east. Buildings are few and mostly frame dwellings, with a storage building near the creek, a post office on Boonton Road, a store and dwelling block at the junction, and the Montville Hotel on the south side of Boonton Road west of Sioux Road. The part is separated from parts 1 and 2 of the sheet, which show Myrtle Avenue in Boonton, by heavy lines, and it adjoins sheet 17, which shows the rest of Montville. Block numbers 169, 169A, 170 and 171 are marked.
notes: Boonton Road is today Main Road and Sioux Road is River Road (OpenStreetMap); the part is anchored on their junction (hand-picked) with north taken from the arrow and the sheet scale.

50 ft. Three parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (top): Myrtle Av with the Van Raalte Co. silk mill and Standard Oil Co., Boonton. Part 2 (lower left): Myrtle Av with the D.L.&W. R.R., Zamium Corp., Boonton Molding Co. Part 3 (lower right): Montville, Boonton Rd (Main Road) at Sioux Rd (River Road), Morris Canal and plane railway.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: upper part: Myrtle Avenue with the Van Raalte Co. silk mill and Standard Oil Co. (no street junction and no feature identified on a placed neighbour; drawn about 24 degrees from the modern line of Myrtle Avenue; needs parcel corners of the Van Raalte site or a feature shared with sheet 15 (step 6b)).

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 shows the village of Montville at 100 feet to an inch, with north up. Boonton Road runs across the lower part of the sheet from west to east, bending north-east at the east edge, and Taylortown Road runs north from it across the double track of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, which crosses the sheet diagonally with its right of way and the railroad station at Taylortown Road. Below the railroad lie the works of the Montville Finishing Company, bleachers, dyers and finishers, with dye houses, a bleach house, a frame house and make-up rooms beside a pond and the creek that runs across the sheet from west to east, three store houses served by sidings, and a wide mill pond to the east. Along Taylortown Road and Boonton Road are the Excelsior Fire Company's fire department, the town hall, the Montville M. E. Church, the Montville Public School, an auto repair shop, the Montville Hotel and frame dwellings with lot numbers. In the south-east corner the Morris Canal and its plane railway, with a gate house, cross the sheet. Large parts of the sheet are open, with block numbers 209 to 213.
notes: Boonton Road is today Main Road (US 202).

Anchored on Main Road / Taylortown Road with the sheet scale and the measured street directions; the railroad crossing on Taylortown Road was left out because the modern line, on a bridge, put the scale 7 percent and the rotation 12 degrees off.
100 ft. Montville: Boonton Rd (Main Road), Taylortown Rd, D.L.&W. R.R. and station, Montville Finishing Co. One part.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18, drawn at 200 feet to an inch, shows the eastern edge of the Mountain Lakes development and the open land between it and Boonton. A turned sheet: streets run across the page at about thirty degrees. The upper left holds the platted blocks of a residential subdivision, lettered C2, D2, E2, F1, F2, G2, H2, I1, I2 and J2, with numbered lots on narrow frontages, along Hanover, Melrose, Oakland and Kenilworth Roads and Cobb Road. Many lots are vacant and few dwellings are drawn. Powerville Road leaves the subdivision at the lower left and runs south-west to Morris Avenue, where the sheet ends in a gas and water pipe at the bottom edge. Boulevard East and Elcock Avenue curve round the head of the subdivision to Reserve Street, Dover Street and Essex Avenue at the top right, the line of Essex Avenue then running south-west to meet Fanny Road. Fanny Road runs down the page to Morris Avenue, where the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the lower right corner in a cutting and the works at the bottom are drawn: Standard Railway Fuse Corporation, Langdon McCormick Studios and the Boonton Gas Light Improvement Company, with a larger plant of unlabelled industrial buildings below Morris Avenue. A large part of the centre is blank, belonging to land not yet built on, and the neighbouring sheets 19, 20, 8, 7 and 6 are named on the margins.
notes: Elcock Avenue, Dover Street and Reserve at the top join sheet 8; Elcock Avenue and the curve of Boulevard East appear to be part of Powerville Road today.
The detector's fit has a root-mean-square residual of about 6 m because the subdivision roads (Hanover, Melrose, Oakland, Kenilworth) do not follow the drawn lines closely; confidence is low.
Street names read from the 1600 px overview; small lot numbers and pipe annotations not transcribed.

200 ft. Mountain Lakes east (Lowell Av, Cobb Rd, Boulevard East, Hanover, Melrose, Oakland, Kenilworth, Powerville Rd) and south Boonton (Morris Av, Fanny Rd, Essex Av, Reserve, Dover St, Elcock Av). Weak fit: subdivision roads carry 5 to 9 m residuals.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19, drawn at 200 feet to an inch, covers the middle of the Mountain Lakes residential development around Wildwood Lake. A turned sheet, with north about thirty degrees east of the page's vertical. At the upper right the platted lettered blocks F, F1, C2, D2 and E2 meet the right edge, where Cobb Road, Hanover Road, Melrose Road and Kenilworth Road continue onto sheet 18, and Glen Road runs south along the lake. The long curve of the Boulevard crosses the sheet from the left to the upper centre, past blocks A, A1 and B, with Laurel Hill Road, Martins Lane, Oak Lane, Barton Road and Lake Drive branching from it. Wildwood Lake fills the centre; a larger unnamed lake lies at the left edge and a stream drains to it near Mountain Lakes Public School and the Mountain Lakes Club. Briarclyffe Road runs north to south along the lake's west shore. The south half is a dense grid of blocks D to W with Larchdell Way, Dartmouth Road, Hillcrest Road, Bellvale Road, Howell Road, The Ball and Elm Road leading down to Morris Avenue, with the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad and the Mountain Lakes railroad station across the bottom. Dwellings are drawn at moderate density, and many lots, especially in the lower-right blocks, are still empty. Water pipe is shown on most streets.
notes: 'Briarclyffe R'd' corresponds to Briarcliff Road and North Briarcliff Road today; the street printed 'Laurel Hill R'd' at the top is North Briarcliff Road in the OpenStreetMap extract; 'Boulevard' and 'Glen R'd' keep their names.
'The Ball' is printed as a street name with 'R'D' on the far side of a junction dot; it may read as The Ball Road, so only the printed words are given.
The fit is a first-order polynomial, root-mean-square about 3.5 m, higher on the curving roads; the Boulevard junctions did not detect and are not used.
Street names read from the 1600 px overview and from a full-resolution crop of the lower left.
200 ft. Mountain Lakes centre: Wildwood Lake, Boulevard, Lake Drive, Midvale, The Ball, Pollard, Romaine, Morris Av and many subdivision roads.

sheet-20-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 20 is the lower strip of the sheet, below the heavy dividing line, drawn at 200 feet to an inch and turned so that streets run across the page. It shows the north-west part of the Mountain Lakes development: blocks lettered D1, E1, G1, H1, I1, J1, K1, L1, M1, N1, O1, P1, Q1, R1, S1 and T1, divided into narrow numbered lots. Four long cross streets run from left to right, Crestview Road West and East near the top, Lookout Road West and East through the middle, Prospect Road and Cobb Road below them, with Mountain Way along the upper left edge, and Tower Hill Road, Ogden Road and Laurel Hill Road at the lower left. Annaaddington Avenue runs north to south across the right half, with Vista Avenue and Laurel Hill Road as the next cross streets to the left. Lowell Avenue and Rock Lane run down the right edge. A handful of dwellings are drawn; most lots are still vacant. Water pipe is marked along Lookout Road and the streets in the lower blocks. The sheet's north arrow points up and to the right. A scale bar at the bottom reads 200 feet to one inch. Sheets 18 and 19 adjoin on the right and below, and sheet 20's upper part, above the dividing line, shows the lakes.
notes: Printed 'Annaaddington Av.' is North Glen Road in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The detector chose a faint-ink setting for this part; the junctions of Crestview Road and Lookout Road are drawn with lines that barely register, and the fit has a root-mean-square of about 3 m.
Mountain Way and Vista Avenue were not matched to OpenStreetMap and are not used for control.
Street names read from the 1600 px overview and two full-resolution crops of the right half.

200 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line: 1 upper, Birchwood, Crystal and Sunset Lakes with Shore Rd (unplaced); 2 lower, Crestview, Lookout, Tower Hill, Ogden, Condit, Laurel Hill, Prospect, Cobb Rd, Annaaddington Av.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: upper part: Birchwood, Crystal and Sunset Lakes, Shore Road (few modern names match and those do not fit the drawing; sheet 21, the neighbour to carry from, has no control on its west side; needs carried points from a better-placed sheet 21 or parcel corners (step 6b)).

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21, drawn at 200 feet to an inch, shows the main body of Mountain Lakes around the lake of the same name, which fills the middle of the page. The sheet is turned about fifty degrees from north. The Boulevard enters at the upper left, runs down the west shore past the blocks P and A, and curves round the southern end of the lake to Lake Drive and Old Denville and Parsipany Road at the bottom. At the upper left are blocks A, B, R3, S3, T3 and U3 with Laurel Hill Road, Tower Hill Road, Glenwood Road, Locust Road, Long View Road, Overlook Road, Cedar Road and Shore Road, and a group of small lakes, Shadow Lake, Olive Lake and Cove Lake, near Crane Road and Sunset Road. The east shore carries the densest platting: blocks J, L, S, Y, Z, R and A between Lake Drive, The Ball, Morris Avenue, Pollard Road and Romaine Road, with Midvale Road at the top and Rockaway Terrace crossing the lower part. Valley Road and Raynold Road run through blocks A2 and A3 at the bottom, where the Denville and Pine Brook Turnpike and the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad cross. Many lots are empty, and dwellings are concentrated along Lake Drive and the Boulevard. A building at the top right is coloured blue. Morris County Traction Company right of way is marked at the lower left.
notes: Printed 'Midvale' at the top and 'Lake Drive' keep their names today; 'Pollard R'd' and 'Romaine R'd' are Pollard Road and Romaine Road.

The Boulevard junctions with Tower Hill Road, Laurel Hill Road and Overlook Road did not detect; the west side has no control points and extrapolates from the east, so the fit (root-mean-square about 4.3 m) is weaker there.
'The Ball' is printed without a suffix in this sheet.
Street names read from the 1600 px overview and a full-resolution crop of the bottom centre.

200 ft, turned on the page. Mountain Lakes south and west: Mountain Lake, Shadow, Olive and Cove Lakes, Boulevard, Lake Drive, Pollard, Valley, Raynold, Morris Av, Denville & Pine Brook Turnpike. Control only on the east shore; the west side extrapolates.
